chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Hammam said:

I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'The slave is returned due to defects of the year, namely insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo. So when you buy a slave and find in him any of these characteristics, between you and the holder of Dhul-Hijjah (i.e., within the year), then return him to his owner.'
Muhammad ibn Ali asked him, 'What if he ran away (abqa)?' He said, 'He is not returned unless he produces evidence that he ran away while in his possession.'

key_terms.أَحْدَاثُ السَّنَةِ: Defects of the year (defects that manifest or are discovered within a year)
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: The holder of Dhul-Hijjah (referring to the specific month used for the one-year period)
key_terms.فَأَبَقَ: He ran away (from the owner's control)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid reasons and time limits for returning a slave due to defects in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of 'ayb' (defects) in commercial transactions, specifically detailing a one-year inspection period for latent conditions like insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo. It further clarifies the evidentiary burden regarding 'abq' (running away), requiring the buyer to prove the defect existed at the time of sale if the slave absconds, thereby protecting the buyer from post-purchase behavioral changes. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on transparency and fairness in trade, ensuring that sellers are accountable for hidden flaws that impair the utility of the commodity.
